school_name: Columbia University in the City of New York
title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Navigate Columbia's diverse academic landscape with these ten distinct study environments, ranging from silent historic reading rooms to modern collaborative hubs.

cards.title: The Silent Standard
cards.subtitle: Butler Library, Room 301
cards.notes: Find a seat at the long wooden tables in this grand, high-ceilinged room. It is strictly silent, making it ideal for deep focus and long reading sessions.
cards.short_summary: A premier silent study hall located on the third floor of Butler Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lawrence A. Wien Reference Room on the third floor is designated for working in absolute silence.
cards.source_title: Your guide to the Columbia libraries depending on your study needs
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 during the academic term; valid CUID required for entry.

cards.title: The Dark Academia Hub
cards.subtitle: Avery Hall
cards.notes: Study among towering bookshelves and classic wooden furniture. The main floor offers a quiet, removed atmosphere perfect for arts and humanities students.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library known for its collegiate aesthetic and quiet communal tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Avery Library's main floor features long coworking tables and is a quiet study space removed from the real world.
cards.access_notes: Check library website for seasonal hours; CUID required.

cards.title: The Modern Glass Box
cards.subtitle: Northwest Corner Building
cards.notes: Utilize this bright, modern space for collaborative work. The floor-to-ceiling windows provide ample natural light and views of the Upper West Side.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary, light-filled library focused on science and engineering research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Science & Engineering Library in the Northwest Corner Building provides a collaborative environment with modern seating.
cards.access_notes: CUID required; group study rooms can be reserved online.

cards.title: The Collaborative Zone
cards.subtitle: Uris Hall
cards.notes: Head here if you prefer a low buzz of conversation while you work. It is one of the few campus libraries where talking and eating are generally permitted.
cards.short_summary: A business-focused library that encourages group work and active discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: The Watson Library is the only library where talking and eating is generally allowed due to the collaborative nature of assignments.
cards.access_notes: Undergraduate access may be restricted during peak finals periods.

cards.title: The Green Chair View
cards.subtitle: Barnard College
cards.notes: Snag a signature green chair facing the floor-to-ceiling windows. This floor offers a mix of individual carrels and open collaborative areas.
cards.short_summary: A popular study floor at Barnard featuring natural light and varied seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of the Milstein Center is known for its green chairs and floor-to-ceiling windows that fill the space with sunlight.
cards.source_title: Study spots on campus to try this finals season
cards.access_notes: Open to both Barnard and Columbia students with valid ID.

cards.title: The Global Affairs Nook
cards.subtitle: International Affairs Building
cards.notes: Work in this spacious library located within the SIPA building. It is excellent for group projects, with several reservable rooms and large tables.
cards.short_summary: A large library in the SIPA building housing social science and map collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehman Social Sciences Library offers group study rooms and a collaborative environment for students.
cards.access_notes: CUID required; located on the 300 level of the IAB.

cards.title: The Quiet Retreat
cards.subtitle: Teachers College, Russell Hall
cards.notes: Climb to the third floor for a strictly quiet study experience. The space is scenic and less frequented by undergraduates from the main campus.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, intensive study space located within the Teachers College library.
cards.evidence_claim: The 3rd floor of the Gottesman Library is a quiet space recommended for intensive study time.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study On Campus!
cards.access_notes: Accessible to Columbia students; check TC-specific hours.

cards.title: The High-Energy Cafe
cards.subtitle: Northwest Corner Building, Lobby
cards.notes: Join the bustle at this popular cafe. It is a prime spot for those who study best with background noise and easy access to caffeine.
cards.short_summary: A vibrant campus cafe with ample seating and a modern aesthetic.
cards.evidence_claim: Joe Coffee in the NoCo building is a classic campus spot where people stay and study for hours.
cards.source_title: Columbia University Northwest Corner Building - Joe Coffee Company
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; seating is first-come, first-served.

cards.title: The Cubicle Corner
cards.subtitle: The Diana Center
cards.notes: Use the desk cubicles on this floor for a sense of privacy. The large windows provide natural light without the heavy traffic of the main libraries.
cards.short_summary: A quieter study area in the Diana Center featuring individual work stations.
cards.evidence_claim: The third floor of the Diana Center has a room filled with desk cubicles and large windows for natural light.
cards.source_title: Study spots on campus to try this finals season
cards.access_notes: Open to Barnard and Columbia students.

cards.title: The Grad Student Sanctuary
cards.subtitle: 302 Philosophy Hall
cards.notes: Reserve this room for student-driven initiatives or quiet study. It is specifically reserved for graduate students, offering a more mature environment.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated seminar and study room for graduate students in Philosophy Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Graduate Seminar Room in 302 Philosophy Hall is available to graduate students with valid CUIDs.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduate students only; booking required for groups.
